paragraphs.title: The Lord Commands Moses to Speak

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in the first verse?
answers: To Moses
To Aaron
To all the children of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “And the Lord spake unto Moses.”

easy.question: To whom was Moses commanded to speak in the second verse?
answers: Only to Aaron
To Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel
Only to all the children of Israel
easy.explanation: Moses was commanded to speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Moses to do?
answers: Build an altar
Leave the land of Israel
Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the children of Israel
easy.explanation: The second verse tells Moses to speak to these three groups.

medium.question: What is the order in which the message is given?
answers: The children of Israel speak to Moses, and Moses speaks to the Lord
The Lord speaks to Moses, and Moses passes the message on to others
Aaron speaks to the Lord, and the Lord speaks to the children of Israel
medium.explanation: First the Lord speaks to Moses; then Moses is commanded to speak to the people.

medium.question: Why are Aaron and his sons, as well as all the children of Israel, mentioned?
answers: To show that the message was only for the priests
To distinguish Moses from Aaron
To make clear that the command was for both the priests and all the people
medium.explanation: The verse names Aaron and his sons along with all the children of Israel, so the message is addressed to both groups.

medium.question: What does “saying” mean in the phrase “the Lord spake unto Moses, saying”?
answers: Speaking or passing on words
Going somewhere else
Remaining silent and listening
medium.explanation: The word “saying” introduces the words that the Lord spoke to Moses.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses was commanded to speak to all the children of Israel as well?
answers: The message was kept secret between Moses and the priests
The message was intended only for the leaders
The message was important for the entire community, not just its leaders
challenge.explanation: Mentioning all the children of Israel shows that the message was not limited to Moses or the priests.

challenge.question: Who directly received the word of the Lord, and who was to deliver it to the people?
answers: Moses received it and was required to deliver it
Aaron received it and delivered it to Moses
All the children of Israel received the word of the Lord directly
challenge.explanation: The first verse says that the Lord spoke to Moses, and the second says that Moses was to speak to the others.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “This is the thing” introduce?
answers: A story from the distant past
A specific message or command that is about to be given
A statement that there is no need to listen further
challenge.explanation: “This is the thing” introduces a particular and clearly defined command from the Lord.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that Moses was commanded to speak to all the children of Israel as well?
answers: The message was kept secret between Moses and the priests
The message was intended only for the leaders
The message was important for the entire community, not just its leaders
questions.explanation: Mentioning all the children of Israel shows that the message was not limited to Moses or the priests.

questions.question: Who directly received the word of the Lord, and who was to deliver it to the people?
answers: Moses received it and was required to deliver it
Aaron received it and delivered it to Moses
All the children of Israel received the word of the Lord directly
questions.explanation: The first verse says that the Lord spoke to Moses, and the second says that Moses was to speak to the others.

questions.question: What does the phrase “This is the thing” introduce?
answers: A story from the distant past
A specific message or command that is about to be given
A statement that there is no need to listen further
questions.explanation: “This is the thing” introduces a particular and clearly defined command from the Lord.

paragraphs.title: Sacrifices Are to Be Offered Only Before the Lord

easy.question: Which animals are mentioned in verse 3?
answers: An ox, a lamb, and a goat
A dove, a turtledove, and an eagle
A camel, a donkey, and a horse
easy.explanation: The verse mentions “an ox, or lamb, or goat.”

easy.question: Where must the offering be brought?
answers: Into the field
To the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
To the king’s house
easy.explanation: The verses command that the offering be brought to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.

easy.question: What does the priest do with the blood of the offering?
answers: Pours it out outside the camp
Drinks it
Sprinkles it upon the altar of the Lord
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that the priest sprinkles the blood upon the altar of the Lord.

medium.question: How is a person regarded if he slaughters an animal but does not bring it to the door of the tabernacle?
answers: As though he had shed blood
As though he had performed a special commandment
As though he had prepared an ordinary meal
medium.explanation: The verse says, “blood shall be imputed unto that man; he hath shed blood.”

medium.question: What is the main purpose of bringing the sacrifices to the tabernacle?
answers: To allow everyone to eat alone in the field
To center sacrificial worship before the Lord through the priest
To replace all sacrifices with gifts to the poor
medium.explanation: The Israelites were to bring their sacrifices to the tabernacle, where the priest offered them to the Lord.

medium.question: What does “sweet savour” mean in the phrase “burn the fat for a sweet savour unto the Lord”?
answers: A bad smell from smoke
A loud sound heard from far away
A pleasing and pleasant smell
medium.explanation: In this context, “sweet savour” means a pleasing smell associated with the offering to the Lord.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the prohibition applying both “in the camp” and “out of the camp”?
answers: The prohibition applies everywhere, not only inside the camp
The prohibition applies only to the priests
The prohibition applies only during wartime
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both places emphasizes that the command cannot be avoided by slaughtering an animal elsewhere.

challenge.question: What is meant by the phrase “unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring” in verse 7?
answers: They follow herds of goats
They turn toward foreign powers or idols
They search for new pasture
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes turning away from the worship of the Lord toward idols or foreign spiritual powers.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in verses 5–6?
answers: The priest burns the fat, then the sacrifice is brought, and finally the blood is sprinkled
The blood is sprinkled in the field, then the fat is eaten, and finally the sacrifice is brought
The sacrifice is brought to the tabernacle, the priest sprinkles the blood, and then burns the fat
challenge.explanation: First the sacrifice is brought to the tabernacle, then the priest sprinkles the blood, and finally burns the fat.

questions.question: What can we infer from the prohibition applying both “in the camp” and “out of the camp”?
answers: The prohibition applies everywhere, not only inside the camp
The prohibition applies only to the priests
The prohibition applies only during wartime
questions.explanation: Mentioning both places emphasizes that the command cannot be avoided by slaughtering an animal elsewhere.

questions.question: What is meant by the phrase “unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring” in verse 7?
answers: They follow herds of goats
They turn toward foreign powers or idols
They search for new pasture
questions.explanation: The phrase describes turning away from the worship of the Lord toward idols or foreign spiritual powers.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in verses 5–6?
answers: The priest burns the fat, then the sacrifice is brought, and finally the blood is sprinkled
The blood is sprinkled in the field, then the fat is eaten, and finally the sacrifice is brought
The sacrifice is brought to the tabernacle, the priest sprinkles the blood, and then burns the fat
questions.explanation: First the sacrifice is brought to the tabernacle, then the priest sprinkles the blood, and finally burns the fat.

paragraphs.title: Every Offering Must Be Brought to the Tabernacle

easy.question: To whom is the command in these verses addressed?
answers: The children of Israel and the strangers living among them
Only the priests
Only the kings of Israel
easy.explanation: The passage addresses both a person of the house of Israel and a stranger living among them.

easy.question: What kind of offering is mentioned?
answers: Only a meal offering
A burnt offering or a sacrifice
Only a Passover offering
easy.explanation: The verse says, “that offereth a burnt offering or sacrifice.”

easy.question: Where must the offering be brought?
answers: To the offerer’s house
Outside the camp
To the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
easy.explanation: The verse commands that the offering be brought to the door of the tabernacle.

medium.question: What must a person do if he wants to offer a sacrifice to the Lord?
answers: Bring it to the door of the tabernacle of the congregation
Offer it wherever he chooses
Give it to another stranger
medium.explanation: The offering must be brought to the door of the tabernacle to be offered to the Lord.

medium.question: What is the punishment for someone who does not bring the offering to the door of the tabernacle?
answers: He must bring a meal offering
He is cut off from among his people
He becomes a priest
medium.explanation: The verse says that such a person “shall be cut off from among his people.”

medium.question: What does “shall be cut off” mean in this context?
answers: He is invited into the community
He receives a new position
He is punished by being separated from his people
medium.explanation: The phrase describes removal or separation from the community as a punishment.

challenge.question: Who is required to bring the offering to the tabernacle?
answers: Both Israelites and strangers living among them
Strangers only
The priests only
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly includes both people of Israel and strangers who sojourn among them.

challenge.question: What central idea can be inferred from these commands?
answers: Only a sacrifice may be offered
Offerings to the Lord must be made at the appointed place
Only wealthy people may offer sacrifices
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize that both burnt offerings and sacrifices must be brought to the door of the tabernacle.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “whatsoever man there be” emphasize?
answers: The command applies only to one particular person
The command is addressed only to leaders
The command applies to every individual in the group
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that every Israelite and every stranger among them is subject to the command.

questions.question: Who is required to bring the offering to the tabernacle?
answers: Both Israelites and strangers living among them
Strangers only
The priests only
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly includes both people of Israel and strangers who sojourn among them.

questions.question: What central idea can be inferred from these commands?
answers: Only a sacrifice may be offered
Offerings to the Lord must be made at the appointed place
Only wealthy people may offer sacrifices
questions.explanation: The verses emphasize that both burnt offerings and sacrifices must be brought to the door of the tabernacle.

questions.question: What does the phrase “whatsoever man there be” emphasize?
answers: The command applies only to one particular person
The command is addressed only to leaders
The command applies to every individual in the group
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that every Israelite and every stranger among them is subject to the command.

easy.question: What are the people forbidden to eat?
answers: Blood
Dust
Flesh
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly command, “Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh.”

easy.question: Who is forbidden to eat blood?
answers: The priests only
The children of Israel and the stranger living among them
Hunters only
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly includes both the children of Israel and the strangers living among them.

easy.question: What should be done with the blood of a hunted animal or bird?
answers: Keep it in a vessel
Put it on the altar
Pour it out and cover it with dust
easy.explanation: The command is to pour out the blood and cover it with dust.

medium.question: Why does the Torah forbid eating blood?
answers: Because the life of the flesh is in the blood, and it is given for atonement on the altar
Because blood is difficult to find
Because only priests know how to cook it
medium.explanation: The passage explains that the life is in the blood and that it was given upon the altar to make atonement.

medium.question: What does “shall be cut off” mean in the phrase “whosoever eateth it shall be cut off”?
answers: He will be blessed
He will be punished by being removed from the community
He will be eaten
medium.explanation: Here, “shall be cut off” describes the punishment of being cut off or separated from the community.

medium.question: What is the correct order after hunting an animal or bird that may be eaten?
answers: Cover it with dust and then pour out the blood
Eat the blood and then cover it
Pour out the blood and then cover it with dust
medium.explanation: The verse gives the order: first pour out the blood, and then cover it with dust.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the fact that the blood is given upon the altar “to make an atonement”?
answers: Blood has a sacred and symbolic role, not merely a role as food
Blood may be eaten only outside the temple
Blood is mainly intended for coloring
challenge.explanation: The connection between blood, the altar, and atonement shows that blood has sacred significance and is not ordinary food.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “any beast or fowl that may be eaten” emphasize alongside the command to cover the blood?
answers: The animal’s flesh may not be eaten
The flesh may be eaten, but its blood may not
Only birds may be eaten
challenge.explanation: The animal or bird is permitted as food, but its blood is still forbidden.

challenge.question: What repeated idea in these verses explains why blood is not food?
answers: Blood is found only in livestock
Blood must always remain in a vessel
Blood is connected with the life of every living creature
challenge.explanation: The verses say that the life of all flesh is in its blood, so blood represents the creature’s life and is not meant to be eaten.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that the blood is given upon the altar “to make an atonement”?
answers: Blood has a sacred and symbolic role, not merely a role as food
Blood may be eaten only outside the temple
Blood is mainly intended for coloring
questions.explanation: The connection between blood, the altar, and atonement shows that blood has sacred significance and is not ordinary food.

questions.question: What does the phrase “any beast or fowl that may be eaten” emphasize alongside the command to cover the blood?
answers: The animal’s flesh may not be eaten
The flesh may be eaten, but its blood may not
Only birds may be eaten
questions.explanation: The animal or bird is permitted as food, but its blood is still forbidden.

questions.question: What repeated idea in these verses explains why blood is not food?
answers: Blood is found only in livestock
Blood must always remain in a vessel
Blood is connected with the life of every living creature
questions.explanation: The verses say that the life of all flesh is in its blood, so blood represents the creature’s life and is not meant to be eaten.

paragraphs.title: Uncleanness and Responsibility When Eating an Animal That Died or Was Torn

easy.question: Who is subject to these laws if he eats an animal that died or was torn?
answers: Everyone, both native-born and stranger
The priests only
The children of Israel only
easy.explanation: The verse applies the law both to a person of the nation and to a stranger.

easy.question: What must the person do after eating such an animal?
answers: Bring an offering immediately
Wash his clothes and bathe in water
Fast until evening
easy.explanation: The verse commands him to wash his clothes and bathe himself in water.

easy.question: Until when does the person remain unclean?
answers: Until morning
Until the end of the week
Until evening
easy.explanation: The verse says that he is unclean until evening, and then he becomes clean.

medium.question: What does the phrase “that which died of itself, or that which was torn with beasts” describe?
answers: An animal that died or was not fit for ordinary eating
An animal that had just been born
An animal dedicated as an offering
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to an animal that died on its own or was torn by other animals.

medium.question: What happens if the person does not perform the required washing and bathing?
answers: He becomes clean immediately
He must leave the camp
He bears his iniquity
medium.explanation: The verse says, “then he shall bear his iniquity,” if he does not wash and bathe.

medium.question: What is the correct sequence according to the verses?
answers: He becomes clean, eats, and then bathes
He eats, washes and bathes, and remains unclean until evening
He bathes, eats, and then becomes unclean
medium.explanation: The passage describes eating first, followed by washing and bathing, and uncleanness until evening.

challenge.question: What precise conclusion can we draw from the verse mentioning both a native-born person and a stranger?
answers: The stranger is exempt from the law
The law applies only during the temple period
The obligation applies to both kinds of people
challenge.explanation: Mentioning both groups shows that the instruction is not limited to native Israelites.

challenge.question: What is the difference between obeying and failing to obey the instructions?
answers: By obeying, the person becomes clean; by failing, he bears iniquity
By obeying, the person is punished; by failing, he becomes clean
In both cases, the person becomes clean immediately
challenge.explanation: The verse describes cleansing after washing and bathing, but says that failure to do so causes the person to bear his iniquity.

challenge.question: What important detail can easily be missed in the phrase “until the even: then shall he be clean”?
answers: Bathing alone makes him clean immediately
Even after bathing, he remains unclean for a limited time
The uncleanness lasts throughout the entire night
challenge.explanation: The verse says that he remains unclean until evening, so bathing does not immediately end the period of uncleanness.

questions.question: What precise conclusion can we draw from the verse mentioning both a native-born person and a stranger?
answers: The stranger is exempt from the law
The law applies only during the temple period
The obligation applies to both kinds of people
questions.explanation: Mentioning both groups shows that the instruction is not limited to native Israelites.

questions.question: What is the difference between obeying and failing to obey the instructions?
answers: By obeying, the person becomes clean; by failing, he bears iniquity

In both cases, the person becomes clean immediately
questions.explanation: The verse describes cleansing after washing and bathing, but says that failure to do so causes the person to bear his iniquity.

answers: Bathing alone makes him clean immediately

The uncleanness lasts throughout the entire night
questions.explanation: The verse says that he remains unclean until evening, so bathing does not immediately end the period of uncleanness.
